title: 2019 Visual Booklet on Pollinators and Pesticides: Keeping Our Bees Safe
claim: Widely used pesticides such as neonicotinoids harm bee health, and UNEP recommends farmers eliminate bee-harming pesticides, plant native flowering plants that provide nectar and pollen through the bloom season, and build nesting sites to help pollinators thrive.
evidence_text: UNEP's booklet on pollinators and pesticides reports that neonicotinoids, among the world's most widely used insecticides, can affect honey bee reproduction and colony health. To make agriculture more bee-friendly, UNEP recommends that farmers eliminate bee-harming pesticides, plant native flowering species that provide nectar and pollen throughout the bloom season, and build nesting sites, recognising that more than three-quarters of food crops rely at least partly on insect and animal pollination.
